verdict: Qualified candidate — modest but real, and honestly bounded. The fail-closed gate did the ordinary job it was built for (the proposal says so and does not claim otherwise), but the activation genuinely exposed a gap one step downstream: the only recovery the loop prescribes for a partial refusal is a full step-8 rerun, which spends a capped doc-drift trial run on an already-sampled round and overwrites the passing critics' same-round artifacts, while the narrower recovery that actually succeeded this round (re-run only the refused critic under the same round id, base and prompt against an unchanged HEAD) is written down nowhere and had to be improvised. Every citation I could check resolves: SKILL.md step 8 dispatches all three passes unconditionally and prescribes only 'rerun /review'; reserve_trial_run counts 'reserved' lines with no slug+round idempotence check; the artifact publish is os.replace over a same-round path; the story's round-7 section records the refused 23-command attempt and the lone-critic retry that promoted. The competing explanation (deliberate simplicity, cap slack, analysis-time dedupe, pre-judgment replacement) is a real one, not a straw man, and the proposal's weakeners are well-chosen. Thomas should treat this as a candidate lesson; the stakes are small and the remedy would go through the review skill's own loop anyway.
contrary_evidence_omitted: One material omission, in the very ledger the proposal cites: the same day (2026-09-21, 14:56), the loop-occurrence-walk round bb30ad7 in claude-light-workflow reserved a doc-drift run whose outcome was 'stopped' with artifact null — a trial reservation consumed by an ordinary trial failure, no rerun involved. This cuts both ways and deserved weighing: it weakens the framing that the full-rerun recovery is the distinctive threat to the 20-run cap (ordinary stops burn runs too), and it bears directly on the proposal's own open frequency question (two failure-flavoured trial events in the trial's first days, not one). Also, evidence item 4 is framed as 'the ledger before this round's recovery: 6 of 20 runs reserved', but the sixth reservation (loop-occurrence-walk, 14:56) postdates this round's recovery (13:38); at the recovery decision the ledger held 5 of 20. The load-bearing sub-claim — every reserved run is a distinct slug+round, so a full rerun would have been the first double-sample — is true under either count, so the lesson is unaffected; the framing is slightly off.
stronger_explanation: none — the proposal's explanation is the best available. The competing explanation it offers is genuinely competing (cap slack plus the fact that the ledger keys every run by slug and round, so a future trial analysis can drop a duplicate, and same-round artifact replacement happens before step 9 judges anything), but its strongest mitigation is hypothetical — no trial analysis exists yet to dedupe — and it does not answer the part of the lesson that actually bit this round: the narrower recovery is undocumented, so the next builder facing a partial refusal must either burn a capped run or improvise without guidance.

findings.title: Evidence item 4's 'before this round's recovery' count includes a later reservation
findings.claim: The proposal describes the ledger state 'before this round's recovery' as '6 of 20 runs reserved', but the sixth reserved line (claude-light-workflow loop-occurrence-walk, 2026-09-21T14:56) is timestamped after this round's doc-drift outcome (13:38) and therefore after the recovery decision; at the decision the ledger held 5 of 20. The substantive claim the citation exists to support — each reserved run is a distinct slug+round, so a full rerun would have been the first round sampled twice — is accurate under either count, and the '14 of 20 left' slack figure in the competing explanation becomes 15, so nothing about the lesson changes. But the citation as worded does not resolve to what it claims about timing.
findings.correction: Reword to separate observation time from decision time, e.g. 'the ledger at the recovery decision: 5 of 20 runs reserved, each on a distinct slug and round; 6 of 20 as read at proposal time' — or drop 'before this round's recovery' and date the read plainly.

findings.title: Same-day stopped trial run in the cited ledger is not weighed
findings.claim: The ledger the proposal cites contains a same-day loop-occurrence-walk entry whose doc-drift outcome is 'stopped' with artifact null — a reservation consumed by an ordinary trial failure with no rerun anywhere in sight. The proposal's isolated-or-systematic section frames the full-rerun recovery as the salient mechanism by which the cap is wasted, and its open question is the frequency of partial refusals; this entry is direct evidence that the cap is also consumed by ordinary stops, and it is a second failure-flavoured trial event within the trial's first days, which bears on the frequency question the proposal leaves open.
findings.correction: Add one line to 'Isolated or systematic' acknowledging the stopped run: it neither strengthens nor weakens the mechanism claim, but it shows trial-cap consumption is not specific to the recovery path the lesson targets, and it should inform how much weight Thomas puts on the cap-cost half of the lesson versus the undocumented-recovery half.
